name: Modern SEO - M3L1 What the Core 30 Framework Is
body:
> Lesson · 2026-10-22

Part of: [Modern SEO - Module 3 Core 30](lib:brain-modern-seo-module-3-core-30) | [Modern SEO Course](lib:brain-modern-seo-course) | [Learning Index](lib:brain-learning-index)

# Summary
Core 30 (4:27) is the advanced system for competitive markets: "building a page on your website for every single category and every single service listed on your Google Business Profile," structured and internally linked the way the GBP is organized. Goal: "massive topical relevance."

# Key concepts
- **When to use it:** three-step method done correctly, some gains, then stuck below 10 to 15% green after 8 to 10 weeks. Typically markets over 500,000 people or with several strong competitors that already have comprehensive sites.
- **Three page levels:**
  - Home page: primary GBP category + city (for example Plumber Houston).
  - Category pages: one per secondary GBP category (for example Drain Cleaning Service, Gas Line Installation).
  - Service pages: one per GBP service under its category (for example Emergency Drain Cleaning, Main Sewer Line Cleaning).
- **Internal linking mirrors the GBP:** home links to all category pages plus one or two critical services (example: water heater replacement); categories link to their services; services link back to their category and home.
- **URL structure does not matter.** "Google works on internal links."
- **Fundamentals first (the "lobby test"):** if a site has many indexed URLs (example: 450) and still ranks 20+ for its primary keyword from the business lobby, Core 30 is not the fix. Look for technical, authority or other fundamental problems.
- **When to stop:** at about 20 to 40% green, topical relevance is usually enough; shift to geographic relevance (neighborhoods and landmarks).
- A PowerPoint template on the course page maps GBP categories and services to pages.

# Checklist
- Trigger met; fundamentals ruled out.
- Home page targets primary category + city.
- One category page per secondary category; one service page per GBP service.
- Links: home to categories (plus critical services), categories to services, services back up.
- Rank map re-checked; switch to geographic relevance at 20 to 40%.

# How this applies to TAG clients
- Before proposing Core 30 for [Pipeliners (Hub)](lib:brain-pipeliners-hub), [Alphalete Trenchless (Hub)](lib:brain-alphalete-trenchless-hub) or [Summit Plumbing Pros AZ (Hub)](lib:brain-summit-plumbing-pros-az-hub), compare the current rank map to the trigger.
- **Alphalete fundamentals gate:** Kim's memory records only 3 of 244 pages indexed in June 2026, with orphaned /services/ city pages and sitemap problems. By this lesson's rule, indexing comes first; confirm current status in [Google Search Console](lib:brain-google-search-console) (see [GSC Indexing Tracker](lib:brain-gsc-indexing-tracker)).
- **Summit AZ fits the lesson's own plumbing examples** almost directly.
- Map each [Google Business Profile](lib:brain-google-business-profile) to the three levels. Focus recommendations on internal links, not URL changes; they go to Kim as a list.

# Caveats and open questions
- "Core 30" as a name is never explained (M3L3 says most businesses need 15 to 25 pages).
- The 450 URL lobby example may be an illustration, not a threshold. The 500,000 population figure has no source.
- The PowerPoint template must be downloaded from the course page.
